Accepts the same JSON body as ``POST /api/v1/search``. The use case
authorizes the actor first, runs the structured provider to get the

    dependencies: Search port bundle for the session.
    correlation: Request correlation id, carried into the ranking

    search (``CaseSearchResponse``).

    Unsupported operator or non-searchable field raises 400;
    an actor without ``case.read`` raises 403 via the domain
    error handler.

post.summary: Draft a new WorkflowVersion (FM-013 / FR-015)
post.description:
Draft a new ``WorkflowVersion`` for an existing ``WorkflowDefinition``.

The validator runs at draft time so a malformed definition is
rejected before any row is persisted. Idempotency: re-drafting the
same body creates a new version row (version_number monotonically
increases). Publishing the draft flips status atomically; the
draft itself is never mutated after creation.

post.summary: Validate a workflow definition without persisting
post.description:
Run the workflow validator over a candidate ``definition``.

The validator is a pure function over the domain entity — no
persistence side effects. The endpoint exists so the admin UI can
preview a definition before committing a draft. The response
carries the parsed ``state_keys`` / ``transition_keys`` so the UI
can render the normalized form.

Authorization is the same ``Action.WORKFLOW_PUBLISH`` check the
draft endpoint enforces; we fail closed (R3 / R12).

post.summary: Validate and publish a draft WorkflowVersion
post.description:
Validate + publish a draft ``WorkflowVersion``.

Re-publishing an already-published version raises
``InvariantViolation`` (mapped to ``409 Conflict``) because the
row's status is no longer ``draft``. The HTTP boundary commits
once after the use case returns so the status flip, the
current-version pointer, and the audit row land atomically
(Constitution IV / plan §4.R12).

post.summary: Dry-run a WorkflowVersion against a synthetic case (FM-015 / P02-US5)
post.description:
Simulate ``WorkflowVersion`` ``version_number`` of workflow ``workflow_id``.

The endpoint is **read-only** -- it never mutates the version, never
persists the synthetic case, and never writes audit or outbox
rows. It is the dry-run companion to the runtime
``execute_transition`` engine.

Authorization mirrors the rest of the admin workflow surface:
``Action.WORKFLOW_PUBLISH`` (granted to ``process_admin``). The
endpoint refuses simulation of a **published** version's mutation
surface -- but the simulator itself never mutates anything; the
guard exists so a misuse (e.g. an attacker crafting a body that
carries publish-shaped actions) cannot bypass the workflow
lifecycle gates. Published versions are therefore readable for
simulation just like draft versions; the rejection criterion is
that the simulated ``actions`` list cannot include keys that are
not declared on the version (the simulator surfaces those as
``no_matching_transition`` blockers).

The response carries the initial state, the final state, the
ordered step trace, and the blockers (if any). The trace is
deterministic -- identical inputs produce identical output, which
the tests assert directly.

get.summary: Defensible-deletion evidence report for a case
get.description:
Assemble the per-case chain-of-custody evidence packet.

The report is a snapshot of the system of record at
``generated_at`` (the request's commit clock). It carries:

- The case identity (id, human reference, created_at).
- The published retention policy that authorised the
  disposition decision (id + version_number + published_at +
  published_by).
- Every ``DispositionRequest`` for the case in chronological
  order (pending / approved / rejected all surface so the
  auditor sees the full decision history).
- The bounded audit chain of the disposition-related event
  types so the chain of custody is re-walkable without
  external joins.

A case with no approved disposition is returned with
``disposed=false`` and an empty ``dispositions`` list — the
absence is the proof of "never silent deletion" (P08 §2).

3. Streams the pre-built ZIP archive as ``application/zip``

``bundle=True`` so the action is visible on the chain. The

post.summary: Capture one inbound email as a case document with provenance
post.description:
Capture one inbound email.

Body shape:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "<uuid>",
  "message_id": "<rfc5322 message id>",
  "sender": "alice@example.test",
  "recipients": ["bob@example.test"],
  "subject": "Hello",
  "case_id": "<uuid>",
  "body_b64": "<base64 of RFC 5322 bytes>"
}
```

Returns ``201`` on a fresh capture and ``200`` (with ``replayed: true``)
on a duplicate ``Message-Id``. The ``Idempotency-Key`` header is
required by the middleware for the 201 path; replays return the
prior response verbatim.

422.description: Invalid payload (empty Message-Id, oversized body, etc.)

post.summary: Capture one scanned page with its scan-result verdict (Gated)
post.description:
Capture one scanned page + its scan-result verdict.

Body shape:

```json
{
  "channel_id": "<uuid>",
  "device_id": "scanner-floor-2",
  "source_label": "Intake counter — 2026-09-02",
  "scan_result": "clean" | "infected" | "inconclusive",
  "scan_detail": "<free-text finding>",
  "case_id": "<uuid>",
  "content_b64": "<base64 of scan bytes>"
}
```

A clean scan releases the quarantine record and produces a
``Document`` on the case in one transaction. An infected /
inconclusive scan keeps the ``QuarantineRecord`` in ``HELD`` and
returns ``released=false`` with no document — the operator
resolves it via ``/api/v1/admin/quarantine/{id}/release|reject``.

403.description: Scan capture is gated off, or actor lacks admin.tenant_config

422.description: Invalid payload (empty bytes, unknown scan_result, etc.)

post.summary: Receive one authorized inbound webhook command
post.description:
Receive one inbound webhook command.

Headers:

- ``X-Webhook-Signature: sha256=<hex>`` — HMAC-SHA256 over
  ``f"{timestamp}.{body}"`` with the channel's shared secret.
- ``X-Webhook-Timestamp: <unix-epoch>`` — replay window of 5 min.
- ``X-Webhook-Id: <stable producer id>`` — durable idempotency
  anchor (the resource-level key, not the HTTP
  ``Idempotency-Key``).
- ``X-Webhook-Source: <producer label>`` — provenance label for
  the audit chain. Defaults to the channel key.
- ``Idempotency-Key: <uuid>`` — request-level replay key (HTTP
  middleware).

Body:

```json
{
  "command_kind": "case.transition",
  "case_id": "<uuid>",
  "payload": {"transition_key": "submit_for_review", "target_state": "in_review"}
}
```

401.description: HMAC verification failed (signature, timestamp, or channel secret)

post.description:
Register a new outbound webhook subscription.

Headers: ``Idempotency-Key`` is required (AGENTS.md §10). The
subscription is created in the same transaction as the
``WebhookSubscriptionRegistered`` audit row so a partial commit
never leaves a subscription without provenance.

patch.description:
Update a subscription with optimistic concurrency.

The ``If-Match`` header is the conventional way to convey

with the other PATCH endpoints.

post.summary: Replay all dead-lettered deliveries for a subscription
post.description:
Reset all dead-lettered deliveries for a subscription to PENDING.

This is the operator's escape hatch when a subscriber's endpoint
was down for an extended period: the platform dead-letters
deliveries that exhaust the cap; the operator fixes the
endpoint and replays. The replay resets ``attempt_count`` to
zero and state to ``PENDING``; the next dispatcher tick will
re-attempt.

The response returns the subscription (the same shape every
other subscription endpoint returns) so a UI can refresh its
detail panel from the response.

get.summary: Read the live state of a session (idle / lockout / cert status).
get.description:
Return the live state of ``session_id``.

The endpoint requires ``AUDIT_READ`` so non-security callers cannot
enumerate sessions. The application use case enforces the
session-control checks (idle / absolute / lockout) and returns a
structured ``SessionDecision``; the router maps the denial reason
to ``HTTP 401`` or surfaces the live snapshot on success.

post.summary: Privileged-action pre-flight: 200 when the request carries an approved client cert, 403 when it does not.
post.description:
Run the privileged-action pre-flight check.

The endpoint returns ``HTTP 403`` when the request would be
refused — mirroring the status a privileged action itself would
surface so a UI can probe the policy without translating the
structured response. Allowed requests return ``HTTP 200`` with the
same shape so a UI can render the denial reason verbatim when it
chose to call this endpoint and ignore the status code.

post.description:
Approve a client certificate for privileged actions on ``session_id``.

This endpoint is the privileged-access-workstation seam (P11-US11).
Activation requires an explicit product decision (ADR-011 Gated):
flip the grant on ``ROLE_PROCESS_ADMIN`` to expose the surface.

post.summary: Record a failed authentication attempt for ``session_id``.
post.description:
Increment the per-session failure counter.

Why this is a public endpoint: the IdP adapter publishes
authentication outcomes via this seam. The endpoint requires
``AUDIT_READ`` (the same shape the audit report does) so only
authorized callers — i.e. the IdP adapter or a process
administrator replaying the synthetic seed — can submit failures.

post.summary: Record a successful authentication for ``session_id``.
post.description:
Clear the per-session failure counter and bump the idle clock.

The IdP adapter publishes successful authentication outcomes via
this seam. The endpoint requires ``AUDIT_READ``; activation is the
same as ``/authentication-failures``.

post.summary: Replace the tenant's published session policy. Gated per ADR-011 (Action.SESSION_POLICY_PUBLISH); no role grants this action today.
post.description:
Publish the tenant's session policy (idle / lockout / privileged actions).

Gated per ADR-011: the endpoint requires
``Action.SESSION_POLICY_PUBLISH``; no role grants it. Activation
requires an explicit product decision.

get.summary: Read the tenant's published session policy (defaults if none).
get.description:
Return the tenant's published policy (defaults if none).

Requires ``AUDIT_READ`` so non-administrators cannot enumerate the
tenant's lockout configuration.

post.summary: Issue a time-bounded, reason-bearing break-glass override (P11-US10 / FM-035). Requires process_admin.
post.description:
Mint a new break-glass grant for ``body.target_user_id``.

The endpoint authorizes against ``ADMIN_TENANT_CONFIG`` so only
a process administrator can mint overrides; auditors do not
grant their own. Issue the grant in the **data-owning** tenant
(the tenant whose cases the grantee may access) — the read-side
enforcement looks the grant up there. The use case writes a
``BreakGlassGranted`` audit row carrying the reason, the scope,
and the expiry so the timeline is complete without an extra fetch.

delete.description:
Revoke ``grant_id`` if it exists in the actor's tenant.

Self-revocation is permitted so an actor can shorten their own
window without involving a second administrator. Idempotent:
revoking an already-revoked grant succeeds and writes a flag
row so the timeline shows the second attempt.

get.summary: Read a case in another tenant under an active break-glass grant (P11-US10 / FM-035). The action is audit-flagged.
get.description:
Read ``case_id`` from ``target_tenant_id`` under an override.

Requires an active ``cross_tenant_case_read`` grant for the actor
in the target tenant (minted by that tenant's administrator via
``POST /security/break-glass``). The flagged audit row carries
the grant id, scope, and reason; the response header echoes the
grant id so the override is prominent on the wire too.

400.description: Target is the actor's own tenant

403.description: No active grant for this scope

404.description: Case not found in target tenant

post.description:
Search ``target_tenant_id`` under a ``cross_tenant_search`` grant.

Field-key sets resolve from the *target* tenant's published
schemas (same P05 contract as the standard path); sensitive
snippets follow the actor's *home* sensitive-read grant. The
flagged audit row carries the grant id, scope, reason, and
result count.

post.description:
Place a legal hold on the case.

The use case refuses a second placement with a structured
``HoldAlreadyPresent`` error (409). The case's ``legal_hold``

``legal_holds`` insert and the ``HoldPlaced`` audit row.

case's ``legal_hold`` flag is flipped back to ``False`` in the
same transaction as the ``legal_holds`` update and the
``HoldReleased`` audit row.

get.description:
Return the snapshot of open cases for the supervisor's team.

The report is **read-only**; no audit or outbox row is written
(P12 pillar statement §2: "reports do not modify state"). The
response carries ``generated_at`` so the caller knows exactly
when the system of record was sampled.

get.summary: Overdue-tasks snapshot for the actor's team (P12-US2)
get.description:
Return the snapshot of overdue tasks for the supervisor's team.

A task is overdue iff ``status == 'open'`` AND ``due_at <= now``.
The report is scoped to the actor's queue memberships; a task
assigned to a queue the supervisor does not belong to is invisible.

Persist a controlled declarative custom-report spec.

The admin-only endpoint validates the body against the closed
vocabulary and stamps the actor + tenant + clock onto the
resulting definition so the audit chain always agrees with the
row.

Render the custom report definition against the system of record.

The renderer delegates to the operational reports' team-scope
contract so a custom report cannot widen the actor's team set.

Render and export a custom report as CSV; the export is audited.

Authorization: ``audit.export`` is required (the export action

Return the manager KPI dashboard for the actor's team.

Mounted under the reports prefix so the wire path resolves to
``GET /api/v1/reports/dashboards/operational`` (the spec text

Run a governed GraphQL query for the calling actor.

The narrow set of scopes a break-glass grant may authorize.

CaseSummary.title: CaseSummary
CaseSummary.description:
The canonical case-workspace read shape.

Workspace slots that land in later pillars (assignee, queue,
participants, open tasks, recent documents, recent decisions,
timeline, SLA state) are typed as either a list (``[]`` for
``participants``/``open_tasks``/etc.) or a ``RedactedField`` so the
OpenAPI document reflects what the server actually returns today.

The ``sensitivity`` field carries the case's effective sensitivity
level (inherited from the case type's ``sensitivity_default`` at
creation time). The client uses it to render a case-level
indicator; it never gates access — server-side redaction is the
authoritative mechanism.

The full ``schema_json`` body for a draft version.

Validated by the application-layer validator; if it fails, the
request returns 422 ``validation_failed`` and the row is not
created.

CaseTypeVersionDetail.description:
Full inspect view of one CaseTypeVersion (FM-021 inspect).

Why separate from ``CaseTypeVersionSummary``: the history list
carries only the fingerprint (field keys) so the timeline stays
light; the inspect view carries the full ``schema`` blob plus the
authorship/effective-time lineage (``published_by`` author,
``published_at`` effective time, ``created_at`` draft time) so an
admin can answer "who authored what, when did it take effect,
and what exactly changed" without a second join. The approval
chain (second-admin ``validate`` row + ``change_summary``) lives
on the governance timeline ``GET /admin/publications`` keyed by
the same ``version_id``.

CaseTypeVersionSummary.description:
Per-version entry returned by the history endpoint.

Excludes the full ``schema_json`` blob so the admin UI can render
the publication timeline without downloading every version's field
list. The full schema is fetchable by id.

Response for a successful claim.

``task_id`` is the canonical handle; the full task view is on
``GET /api/v1/tasks/{id}``. The response deliberately omits
the task body so the claim endpoint stays small and the worker
UI fetches the detail on click.

CompleteTaskRequest.description:
POST body for ``/api/v1/tasks/{id}/complete`` (FR-011).

``outcome`` is the structured closure detail (``{"decision":
"approved", "notes": "..."}``). It is recorded on the audit row
and on the aggregate, but never embedded in the outbox payload
(outbox payloads are id-references by policy).

``trigger_transition_key`` is the workflow transition the engine
should fire in the same transaction when the task completes. The
transition's guard is evaluated against the case context; if the
guard fails the entire transaction rolls back so the task is not
committed ``completed`` without its paired transition (Constitution
III / P02-US1 acceptance scenario 1).

ConfigureReferenceFormatRequest.title: ConfigureReferenceFormatRequest
ConfigureReferenceFormatRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/reference-format``.

The ``template`` is the **human-readable** projection only; the
Case's internal UUID identity is unchanged by this endpoint
(Constitution I). Validation runs in the application layer
(``validate_template``) so a malformed template yields
``422 validation_failed`` with a structured error body and is
never persisted.

CorrectionRequest.title: CorrectionRequest
CorrectionRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v1/audit/{event_id}/correction``.

The operator must pass every field explicitly; the API does not
default a ``reason`` or ``corrected_summary``.

CorrectionResponse.title: CorrectionResponse
CorrectionResponse.description:
Response body for ``POST /api/v1/audit/{event_id}/correction``.

``original_event_id`` is the row being annotated; ``new_event_id``
is the appended ``AuditCorrectionRecorded`` row. The store stamps
the id at commit; we surface it so a client can correlate the two
on the timeline.

CreateWorkflowRequest.title: CreateWorkflowRequest
CreateWorkflowRequest.description: Body for creating a workflow definition header.

CustomReportBucketResponse.title: CustomReportBucketResponse
CustomReportBucketResponse.description: One row of a rendered custom-report result (P12-US7).

name.title: Name
name.description: Display name; may be renamed later.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description: Optional filter clauses applied before aggregation.

time_window_hours.title: Time Window Hours
time_window_hours.description: Optional rolling time window in hours.

CustomReportDefinitionResponse.title: CustomReportDefinitionResponse
CustomReportDefinitionResponse.description: The wire shape for the custom-definition create response.

DeclareDisposalFreezeRequest.title: DeclareDisposalFreezeRequest
DeclareDisposalFreezeRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/disposal-freezes``.

``starts_at`` (inclusive) and ``ends_at`` (exclusive) define
the window during which the disposition approval use case
refuses to approve any pending request. ``reason`` is
required.

DelegateRequest.title: DelegateRequest
DelegateRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/tasks/delegate`` (P02-US9 / FM-016).

``until`` is the exclusive bound on the delegation window: the
delegate holds each task while ``now <= until``; once ``now >
until`` the ``expire_delegations`` sweep restores the prior owner.
A past ``until`` is rejected with 409 so a worker cannot hand off
work they no longer own.

DelegateResponse.title: DelegateResponse
DelegateResponse.description:
Response for ``POST /api/v1/tasks/delegate`` (P02-US9 / FM-016).

Echoes the bounded window (``until``) so the worker UI can render
the cover period without re-reading the audit row.

DisposalFreezeResponse.title: DisposalFreezeResponse
DisposalFreezeResponse.description: The wire shape of a :class:`DisposalFreeze` row.

DispositionDecisionRequest.title: DispositionDecisionRequest
DispositionDecisionRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/disposition/{request_id}/approve|reject``.

``reason`` is optional for approval and required for rejection
(the domain ``DispositionRequest.reject`` raises
:class:`ValidationFailed` on a blank reason).

DispositionEvidenceEntry.title: DispositionEvidenceEntry
DispositionEvidenceEntry.description:
A single disposition decision row on the chain of custody.

``status`` carries the decision (``approved`` / ``rejected`` /
``pending``); the report may include every status so the
auditor sees the full history (a rejected request followed by
a later approved one is the norm). ``decided_by`` + ``decided_at``
are populated only when the request is no longer ``pending``;
the field is the actor who recorded the decision (the
aggregate calls this ``reviewed_by``).

DispositionRequestResponse.title: DispositionRequestResponse
DispositionRequestResponse.description: The wire shape of a :class:`DispositionRequest` row.

DocumentRedactionResponse.title: DocumentRedactionResponse
DocumentRedactionResponse.description: The wire shape of a single ``DocumentRedaction`` (P03-US6 / FM-025).

DocumentResponse.title: DocumentResponse
DocumentResponse.description:
The wire shape returned by ``POST /api/v1/cases/{id}/documents``.

Carries the metadata of the persisted document plus the initial
version row so the client can render "v1 of <file>" without a
second round trip. Subsequent versions land via the add-version
endpoint (FM-023 / P03-US2 — deferred).

DocumentSearchHit.title: DocumentSearchHit
DocumentSearchHit.description:
A single document search hit on the wire.

The shape mirrors the ``DocumentSearchHit`` domain shape: the
document identity + metadata, the bounded snippet (``Redacted``
marker when the actor cannot see the content), and the audit
timestamps. The worker can navigate to the document directly via
the case workspace without re-issuing the search.

DocumentSearchResponse.title: DocumentSearchResponse
DocumentSearchResponse.description:
GET ``/api/v1/cases/{id}/documents/search`` response.

Follows the AGENTS.md §17.1 envelope plus an advisory
``total_considered`` so the UI can render an "X results" footer
without a second round-trip.

DocumentSensitivity.title: DocumentSensitivity
DocumentSensitivity.description: A sensitivity label for a document (P11 / P05-US3).

DocumentVersionResponse.title: DocumentVersionResponse
DocumentVersionResponse.description: The wire shape of a single ``DocumentVersion``.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: synthetic | onbase | panzura (named kinds are Gated per ADR-015)

authorization_rationale.title: Authorization Rationale
authorization_rationale.description: Required for named connectors (any kind other than 'synthetic'); the domain refuses to construct the row without it. Optional for synthetic connectors but recommended.

DraftWorkflowVersionRequest.title: DraftWorkflowVersionRequest
DraftWorkflowVersionRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/workflows/{key}/versions``.

The router translates the wire states/transitions into the domain
:class:`WorkflowState` and :class:`WorkflowTransition` dataclasses
before handing them to the use case; the validator runs after that
translation.

EditCaseRequest.title: EditCaseRequest
EditCaseRequest.description:
PATCH body for ``/api/v1/cases/{id}`` (P01-US3).

Every field is optional — only the fields the caller intends to
change are sent. The router pairs this with the required
``If-Match: <version_token>`` header (FR-003 acceptance scenario 3).
A stale ``If-Match`` returns 409 with the current ``version_token``
in the body so the client can refetch and retry.

EligibleCaseEntryResponse.title: EligibleCaseEntryResponse
EligibleCaseEntryResponse.description: A single entry on the eligible-for-disposition list.

channel_id.title: Channel Id
channel_id.description: If supplied, update the existing channel instead of creating one

EventTypeIn.title: EventTypeIn
EventTypeIn.description:
Body shape for a single event type contribution.

``payload_keys`` is the whitelist; anything not in the list is
rejected at publish time (``domain.events.validate_payload``). The
redaction list in ``domain.extension`` rejects PHI-named keys at
registration time so a module with PHI in its schema is blocked
before it ships.

EvidenceBundleRequest.title: EvidenceBundleRequest
EvidenceBundleRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v1/exports/bundle`` (P14-US8 / FM-060).

``case_id`` identifies the case the operator is exporting.
``reason`` is a free-text justification that lands on the audit
chain verbatim — same convention as the structured audit export
(FM-044). ``can_see_sensitive`` is an explicit opt-in: the
default is ``False`` so the bundle ships with restricted fields
redacted; the use case re-evaluates ``CASE_READ_SENSITIVE``
against the actor's role set so a request without the grant is
refused regardless of the flag.

EvidenceReportResponse.title: EvidenceReportResponse
EvidenceReportResponse.description:
The wire shape of ``GET /api/v1/retention/evidence/{case_id}``.

The report declares ``kind="snapshot"`` (P12 §1 — snapshot vs.
aggregate is explicit) and ``generated_at`` so the consumer
knows exactly when the system of record was sampled. The
``disposed`` flag is the compliance signal: ``true`` iff at
least one ``DispositionRequest`` is in ``approved`` status.
Cases without an approved disposition are deliberately
returned with an empty ``dispositions`` list and
``disposed=false`` — the absence from the platform-wide
defensible-deletion log is the proof of "never silent
deletion" (P08 §2).

ExecuteTransitionRequest.title: ExecuteTransitionRequest
ExecuteTransitionRequest.description:
POST body for ``/api/v1/cases/{id}/transitions`` (FR-009).

``transition_key`` is the stable key declared on the workflow
transition (``"submit_for_review"``, ``"record_decision"``).
``payload`` is the caller's structured transition payload — its
keys are surfaced as ``payload.*`` to guard expressions and
recorded on the audit row.

ExecuteTransitionResponse.title: ExecuteTransitionResponse
ExecuteTransitionResponse.description:
POST response for ``/api/v1/cases/{id}/transitions``.

Reports the post-transition state (``from_state`` → ``to_state``)
and the list of follow-on tasks created by the transition's
``create_task`` actions.

ExportBatchResponse.title: ExportBatchResponse
ExportBatchResponse.description: A page of the audit export plus batch metadata (P09-US5 / FM-044).

ExportEntryResponse.title: ExportEntryResponse
ExportEntryResponse.description:
A single audit row in the export batch (P09-US5 / FM-044).

Mirrors ``TimelineEntryResponse`` and adds the chain anchors the
export consumer needs to verify integrity off-system. The payload
is redacted through the same allowlist as the timeline; the
``hash`` / ``prev_hash`` fields are integrity metadata, not
payload content, and are not redacted.

ExtensionEventCatalog.title: ExtensionEventCatalog
ExtensionEventCatalog.description:
Response shape for ``GET /api/v1/extensions/events/catalog``.

Composes the built-in catalog (``app.domain.events.EVENT_CATALOG``)
with every event type the extensions have registered. Built-in
entries take precedence on duplicate keys; ``source`` is the union
shape documented in ``iter_event_specs``.

ExtensionOut.title: ExtensionOut
ExtensionOut.description:
Catalog entry — the response shape of ``POST /extensions`` and
``GET /extensions``.

ExtensionsCatalog.title: ExtensionsCatalog
ExtensionsCatalog.description:
Response shape for ``GET /api/v1/extensions/catalog``.

The catalog is intentionally flat (not ``Page[T]``); the registry
is bounded by the number of modules a tenant can install. The
``source`` field documents that the entries come from the
process-local registry; FM-047 slice 2 will overlay the persistent
table on top of this.

FieldDefinitionRequest.title: FieldDefinitionRequest
FieldDefinitionRequest.description: Wire shape of a single field on a CaseTypeVersion schema.

source.title: Source
source.description: Source column name in the input row

field.title: Field
field.description: Stable field identifier; must be in the closed allowlist.

op.title: Op
op.description: Filter operator; must be valid for the field.

FormBindingDetailResponse.title: FormBindingDetailResponse
FormBindingDetailResponse.description: Full detail of one form binding.

FormDefinition.title: FormDefinition
FormDefinition.description: The declarative body of a form.

FormFieldSpec.title: FormFieldSpec
FormFieldSpec.description: A single field on a form.

FormSectionSpec.title: FormSectionSpec
FormSectionSpec.description: A grouping of fields on a form.

FormSessionResponse.title: FormSessionResponse
FormSessionResponse.description:
Read-side projection of an in-progress form session.

``progress`` is a list of ``[step_key, status]`` tuples where
``status`` is one of ``pending``, ``current``, ``completed``.

FormStepSpec.title: FormStepSpec
FormStepSpec.description: Resolved step entry returned to the SPA.

FormVersionResponse.title: FormVersionResponse
FormVersionResponse.description: A published form version returned to the client.

GraphQLErrorItem.title: GraphQLErrorItem
GraphQLErrorItem.description:
One entry of the GraphQL ``errors`` array.

``code`` is the platform error code (``forbidden``, ``not_found``,
``validation_failed``); ``message`` is safe to display (never SQL,
secrets, or stack traces); ``path`` is the JSON path of the failing
field (for example ``["case", "documents"]``).

GraphQLRequest.title: GraphQLRequest
GraphQLRequest.description:
The HTTP body for ``POST /graphql``.

``query`` is the raw GraphQL query text (queries only; ``mutation``
operations are rejected by the parser). ``variables`` is accepted
in the schema so clients get a clear 400 instead of a silent drop,
but any non-empty value is rejected because the executor inlines
all arguments and does not resolve variable references.

GraphQLResponse.title: GraphQLResponse
GraphQLResponse.description:
The HTTP wire shape for ``POST /graphql``.

``data`` is the resolved field tree (a denied or missing branch is
``null``); ``errors`` carries per-field denials and root-level
failures. A well-formed execution always returns HTTP 200, even
when ``errors`` is non-empty — the status code describes the
transport, the ``errors`` array describes the policy outcome.

ImportJobListItemResponse.title: ImportJobListItemResponse
ImportJobListItemResponse.description: Minimal job summary for the list endpoint (FM-027).

ImportJobResponse.title: ImportJobResponse
ImportJobResponse.description:
Wire shape of the persisted import job.

The status is exposed so the operator UI can branch on
``previewed`` / ``committed`` / ``failed``.

ImportJobStatus.title: ImportJobStatus
ImportJobStatus.description:
The job lifecycle.

- ``PENDING`` — accepted but not yet processed.
- ``PREVIEWED`` — dry-run completed; the report is attached.
- ``COMMITTING`` — a commit is in flight.
- ``COMMITTED`` — at least one record was accepted; the reconciliation
  report records what was rejected.
- ``FAILED`` — the pipeline aborted before any record was committed.

Why a separate ``COMMITTED`` (not just reusing ``PREVIEWED``): a
committed job is a *terminal* state for the same logical import;
further changes only happen by a new job. The terminal-vs-non-terminal
split drives the operator UI ("is this safe to re-run?").

ImportMappingDetailResponse.title: ImportMappingDetailResponse
ImportMappingDetailResponse.description: Full detail of one import mapping version.

ImportReconciliationResponse.title: ImportReconciliationResponse
ImportReconciliationResponse.description: Wire shape of the reconciliation summary.

ImportRowRequest.title: ImportRowRequest
ImportRowRequest.description:
A single source row.

``index`` is the operator-facing ordinal (1-based). ``values`` maps
source column names to string values.

ImportRowResponse.title: ImportRowResponse
ImportRowResponse.description: Wire shape of a per-row reconciliation entry.

mapping_id.title: Mapping Id
mapping_id.description: Reference a published ImportMapping by id (FM-026). Use this instead of inline 'mapping' when the mapping is registered in the import-mapping registry.

ImportRowsPayload.title: ImportRowsPayload
ImportRowsPayload.description: The body of a dry-run or commit request.

LegalHoldResponse.title: LegalHoldResponse
LegalHoldResponse.description:
The wire shape of a :class:`app.domain.legal_hold.LegalHold` row.

The router serializes the domain aggregate into this shape so
the client sees a stable, Pydantic-typed contract.

LockDocumentResponse.title: LockDocumentResponse
LockDocumentResponse.description:
The wire shape returned by ``POST /api/v1/documents/{id}/lock``.

Carries the locked metadata so the caller can render "locked at/by"
without a second round trip.

MappingVersionRequest.title: MappingVersionRequest
MappingVersionRequest.description:
Wire shape of a versioned mapping document.

The version number is informational on input — the application
layer validates the rest of the document against the case-type
schema before accepting.

retired_case_id.title: Retired Case Id
retired_case_id.description: The case that will be folded in.

MonitorConnectorResponse.title: MonitorConnectorResponse
MonitorConnectorResponse.description: Wire shape of the monitor snapshot.

OpenCaseReportRow.title: OpenCaseReportRow
OpenCaseReportRow.description: One row of the open-cases report (P12-US1 / FM-051).

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Report kind; always "snapshot" for the first slice.

team.title: Team
team.description: Sorted queue keys the report covers (the actor's team).

OpenCasesReportResponse.title: OpenCasesReportResponse
OpenCasesReportResponse.description:
The wire shape for ``GET /api/v1/reports/open-cases``.

``generated_at`` is the system-of-record-as-of timestamp (P12 §1).
``team`` is the sorted list of queue keys the supervisor is a
member of; an empty list means the actor has no team.
``kind`` is always ``"snapshot"`` for the first slice.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Dashboard kind; always "snapshot" for the first slice.

freshness_seconds.title: Freshness Seconds
freshness_seconds.description: Wall-clock gap between generated_at and served_at (FM-054).

team.title: Team
team.description: Sorted queue keys the dashboard covers (the actor's team).

OperationalDashboardResponse.title: OperationalDashboardResponse
OperationalDashboardResponse.description:
The wire shape for ``GET /api/v1/reports/dashboards/operational``.

``generated_at`` is the system-of-record-as-of timestamp the two
snapshot reads were issued against (P12 §1). ``freshness_seconds``
is the gap between ``generated_at`` and ``served_at``; FM-054
promises sub-five-second freshness so the field is capped at 5.
``kind`` is always ``"snapshot"`` — the dashboard is a
point-in-time view, not an aggregate over a window.

OperationalKPIsResponse.title: OperationalKPIsResponse
OperationalKPIsResponse.description:
The KPI payload for ``GET /api/v1/dashboards/operational``.

``open_by_priority`` breaks ``total_open_cases`` down by priority so
the manager can see how much of the load is urgent vs normal.
Unknown priority values are bucketed under ``"other"`` rather than
dropped so a future priority value never silently changes the
total.

OrphanProposalEntryResponse.title: OrphanProposalEntryResponse
OrphanProposalEntryResponse.description: A single entry on the orphan-proposal scan result.

OrphanProposalResponse.title: OrphanProposalResponse
OrphanProposalResponse.description: The wire shape of a :class:`OrphanCaseProposal` row.

OrphanScanResponse.title: OrphanScanResponse
OrphanScanResponse.description:
Wire shape for ``POST /api/v1/admin/orphan-proposals/scan``.

``items`` are the freshly staged proposals. ``skipped_holds``
are the case ids the scan skipped because they were under
active legal hold (the pillar's "hold overrides retention"
invariant is preserved).

retrying.title: Retrying
retrying.description: Pending rows with a recorded failure

OutboxLagSummary.title: OutboxLagSummary
OutboxLagSummary.description:
Lag counters for the operator dashboard.

``pending`` is everything with no ``dispatched_at``; ``dead_lettered``
is the subset that has hit ``MAX_ATTEMPTS`` and will not be retried
automatically; ``retrying`` is rows with a non-null ``last_error``
but still under the cap.

OutboxListResponse.title: OutboxListResponse
OutboxListResponse.description:
Wrapper for the list endpoint.

Mirrors the canonical ``Page[T]`` envelope (AGENTS.md §17.1) so the
operator UI can paginate via the same client.

OutboxReplayResponse.title: OutboxReplayResponse
OutboxReplayResponse.description:
Result of ``POST /admin/outbox/{id}/replay``.

``reset`` is the success path; ``noop`` means the row did not
exist or was already dispatched (the operator UI distinguishes
them so the caller's intent — "retry this row" — is observable.

OutboxRowResponse.title: OutboxRowResponse
OutboxRowResponse.description:
Wire shape of a single outbox row.

The row id is the operator-facing key (it appears in the replay
path). ``is_dead_lettered`` is a derived flag the UI uses to color
the row red — the dispatcher computes it from ``attempt_count``
rather than persisting it on the row.

overdue_seconds.title: Overdue Seconds
overdue_seconds.description: Whole seconds past the due_at at the report's generated_at.

OverdueTaskReportRow.title: OverdueTaskReportRow
OverdueTaskReportRow.description: One row of the overdue-tasks report (P12-US2 / FM-051).

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: Report kind; always "snapshot" for the first slice.

team.title: Team
team.description: Sorted queue keys the report covers (the actor's team).

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Free-text rationale for placing the hold (required).

PlaceHoldRequest.title: PlaceHoldRequest
PlaceHoldRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v1/cases/{id}/holds``.

``reason`` is required so the audit row never carries a
meaningless rationale. The HTTP layer maps ``ValidationFailed``
on a blank reason to 422.

PolicyActionIn.title: PolicyActionIn
PolicyActionIn.description:
Body shape for a policy action contribution.

Mirrors ``app.domain.extension.PolicyActionSpec``; ``is_sensitive``
defaults to False so a safe-by-default request body is also a
valid one.

PolicyEvidenceEntry.title: PolicyEvidenceEntry
PolicyEvidenceEntry.description:
The published policy that authorised the disposition decision.

The wire shape is a flattened snapshot of the
:class:`app.domain.retention.RetentionPolicy` row the use case
resolved for the most-recent approved disposition. The
``version_number`` + ``published_at`` pair is the minimum
evidence a compliance officer needs to confirm "which policy
was active when this record was disposed" (P12 §1 — reports
identify their source timestamp; P08 §2 — defensible
disposition is auditable end-to-end).

client_cert_thumbprint.title: Client Cert Thumbprint
client_cert_thumbprint.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the presented X.509 client certificate; absent when the request carries no cert.

PublicationRecordResponse.title: PublicationRecordResponse
PublicationRecordResponse.description:
A single publication-history row (FM-021).

The wire shape mirrors :class:`PublicationRecord` plus the actor
fields the admin timeline UI needs (``actor_id`` is sufficient for
display; a separate ``/users/{id}`` lookup resolves the display
name).

PublishRetentionPolicyRequest.title: PublishRetentionPolicyRequest
PublishRetentionPolicyRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/retention-policies``.

The policy declares a retention period (``period_days``) for the
chosen ``category`` (``case`` for v1). ``target_key`` scopes the
policy within the category; case-level policies use the empty
string (the tenant default). A non-empty ``target_key`` is
required for ``document`` and ``audit`` categories (the domain
refuses empty keys for those).

idle_timeout_seconds.title: Idle Timeout Seconds
idle_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds of no activity before a session is logged out (max 24h).

absolute_timeout_seconds.title: Absolute Timeout Seconds
absolute_timeout_seconds.description: Maximum session lifetime in seconds (max 7 days).

lockout_duration_seconds.title: Lockout Duration Seconds
lockout_duration_seconds.description: How long a locked session refuses access (max 24h).

privileged_actions.title: Privileged Actions
privileged_actions.description: Action names that require an approved client certificate. Empty by default — adding entries here activates the privileged-action check (Gated per ADR-011).

PublishedCaseTypeField.title: PublishedCaseTypeField
PublishedCaseTypeField.description: A supported, published field definition rendered by intake forms.

PublishedCaseTypeListResponse.title: PublishedCaseTypeListResponse
PublishedCaseTypeListResponse.description: Tenant-scoped published case types for the create-case selector.

PublishedCaseTypeResponse.title: PublishedCaseTypeResponse
PublishedCaseTypeResponse.description: One published case type usable by the authenticated intake actor.

PublishedCaseTypeSchema.title: PublishedCaseTypeSchema
PublishedCaseTypeSchema.description: The declarative schema needed to render and validate intake.

QueueSummary.title: QueueSummary
QueueSummary.description: A queue as returned to admins / workers.

QueueTaskAging.title: QueueTaskAging
QueueTaskAging.description: Worker-facing due-date / aging readout for one queue task.

QueueTaskView.title: QueueTaskView
QueueTaskView.description: One open task on a queue with its aging context (P02-US3 / FM-016).

ReconfigureQueueRequest.title: ReconfigureQueueRequest
ReconfigureQueueRequest.description:
Body for ``PUT /api/v1/admin/queues/{queue_id}``.

Every field is optional; ``None`` means "leave unchanged". An
empty list for ``member_user_ids`` means "clear the membership
list" (only legal under ``manual`` — the aggregate rejects it
under ``round_robin``).

RecordPublicationRequest.title: RecordPublicationRequest
RecordPublicationRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/publications``.

The router is the durable-write seam for the publish lifecycle
(P10-US4) and is called by the existing ``publish_case_type`` /
``publish_workflow`` use cases after the status flip. The HTTP
surface is exposed so the admin UI (and tests) can drive the
approval flow directly.

RedactedField.title: RedactedField
RedactedField.description:
A field whose content the actor is not authorized to see.

The schema is deliberately minimal: ``redacted: true`` plus a
human-readable ``reason``. The client renders ``(restricted)`` or
similar and never sees the underlying content. This is the only
shape a redacted field may take on the wire.

ReferenceFormatResponse.title: ReferenceFormatResponse
ReferenceFormatResponse.description: Body for ``GET`` / ``POST`` / ``DELETE`` on the admin reference-format API.

RelationshipKind.title: RelationshipKind
RelationshipKind.description:
The semantic kind of an edge between two cases (FM-010).

Three kinds cover the P01 user stories:

- ``related`` — symmetric peer association (US5). Stored as one row
  per direction so each case can navigate its peers without a join.
- ``split_from`` — the source case was split into the target case
  (US7). Stored as one row ``(source=original, target=new)``;
  ``original.children`` is just ``list_related(original,
  kind=split_from)``.
- ``merged_into`` — the source case was merged into the target case
  (US8). Stored as one row ``(source=old, target=survivor)``;
  ``old.survivor`` resolves the survivor.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Free-text rationale for releasing the hold (required).

ReleaseHoldRequest.title: ReleaseHoldRequest
ReleaseHoldRequest.description:
Request body for ``DELETE /api/v1/cases/{id}/holds``.

``reason`` is required for the same reason as
:class:`PlaceHoldRequest` — every release carries a rationale
so an auditor can replay the chain and see why the disposition
block was lifted.

queue_key.title: Queue Key
queue_key.description: Return queue. Required when the task was claimed through ``POST /queues/{key}/claim`` (a claim clears the queue pointer); ignored when the task still carries one.

ReportExportResponse.title: ReportExportResponse
ReportExportResponse.description:
The wire shape for ``POST /api/v1/reports/custom/{definition_id}/export``.

``audit_event_id`` is the id of the ``AuditExported`` row the
use case staged so the caller can correlate the export with the
audit chain.

RetentionPolicyResponse.title: RetentionPolicyResponse
RetentionPolicyResponse.description: The wire shape of a :class:`RetentionPolicy` row.

drain_notes.title: Drain Notes
drain_notes.description: Operator's plan / context for the drain.

in_flight.title: In Flight
in_flight.description: Operator-confirmed in-flight count. The use case refuses to retire while in_flight > 0 (Constitution V).

ReviewOrphanProposalRequest.title: ReviewOrphanProposalRequest
ReviewOrphanProposalRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/orphan-proposals/{id}/review``.

``decision`` is either ``"surface"`` or ``"dismiss"``. The
dismissal requires a non-blank ``reason``; surfacing does
not (the rationale is implied by the action).

RoleSummary.title: RoleSummary
RoleSummary.description:
A role as returned to admins.

Excludes the per-permission internal description; callers can
fetch a full record by id if needed.

SaveFormStepRequest.title: SaveFormStepRequest
SaveFormStepRequest.description: PATCH body for saving one step's partial data.

SavedSearchList.title: SavedSearchList
SavedSearchList.description: A list of the actor's saved searches, newest first.

SavedSearchRequest.title: SavedSearchRequest
SavedSearchRequest.description:
POST ``/api/v1/search/saved`` body.

Mirrors the case-search request shape plus the human ``name`` the
worker uses to recall the saved query. ``filters`` and ``sort``
are optional; an empty saved search is a free-text bookmark.

SavedSearchResponse.title: SavedSearchResponse
SavedSearchResponse.description:
A persisted saved search on the wire.

``query_shape`` is the canonical ``{text_query, filters, sort}``
dict the audit row references; the security report can correlate
saves and runs without re-parsing the request.

SearchAuditEntryResponse.title: SearchAuditEntryResponse
SearchAuditEntryResponse.description:
A single search-audit row on the security-report wire shape.

The query shape and the result count are returned verbatim so a
security administrator can answer "who searched for what and saw
how many results" (P06-US5 / FM-032).

SearchAuditList.title: SearchAuditList
SearchAuditList.description: A page of search-audit rows plus the standard envelope.

SearchFilterRequest.title: SearchFilterRequest
SearchFilterRequest.description:
A single fielded filter (``field``, ``op``, ``value``).

``op`` is the controlled vocabulary defined by the application
layer (``eq`` / ``like`` / ``in``). ``value`` is either a string
or a list of strings; the router converts it to the right shape
for the SQL adapter.

SessionDenialReason.title: SessionDenialReason
SessionDenialReason.description:
Stable denial reasons for session-level refusals.

The string values are the on-the-wire contract. Adding a new value
is a wire-incompatible change; deprecating a value requires
acceptance on both client and server.

SessionFailureRequest.title: SessionFailureRequest

SessionState.title: SessionState
SessionState.description:
The lifecycle of a session.

- ``ACTIVE`` — usable; subject to idle / absolute timeout checks.
- ``LOCKED`` — temporarily refused due to lockout.
- ``EXPIRED`` — refused because the idle or absolute window
  elapsed. Distinguished from ``LOCKED`` so the audit timeline can
  report the cause.
- ``REVOKED`` — explicitly terminated (logout, break-glass
  eviction). The session id remains in the durable record for
  audit but the session is no longer usable.

SignedBatchPage.title: SignedBatchPage
SignedBatchPage.description: A page of signed batches (P09-US9 / FM-046).

SignedBatchRequest.title: SignedBatchRequest
SignedBatchRequest.description:
Request body for ``POST /api/v1/audit/signed-batches``.

The operator picks an inclusive event range (``first_event_id``
and ``last_event_id``) and provides a free-text ``reason`` that
is recorded in the batch payload. The chain is verified against
the durable ``audit_events`` table before signing.

SignedBatchResponse.title: SignedBatchResponse
SignedBatchResponse.description:
A tamper-evident batch of audit rows (P09-US9 / FM-046).

The auditor re-reads the rows through the standard audit read
API to verify the chain (P09-US3), then recomputes the signature
using the published ``key_id`` and ``algorithm`` and compares
against ``signature``. ``payload`` is the canonical JSON that
was signed.

SimulateWorkflowVersionRequest.title: SimulateWorkflowVersionRequest
SimulateWorkflowVersionRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/workflows/{id}/versions/{n}/simulate``.

``synthetic_case`` is the case data the guards will be evaluated
against. It is **never** persisted; the endpoint is a dry-run. The
optional ``actions`` list drives deterministic progression: when
omitted, the simulator auto-progresses through the first available
transition at every state.

SimulateWorkflowVersionResponse.title: SimulateWorkflowVersionResponse
SimulateWorkflowVersionResponse.description:
Response for the simulation endpoint.

``outcome`` is ``completed`` / ``blocked`` / ``exception``. ``steps``
is the ordered list of every transition the simulator fired; each
step carries the evaluated guards so the admin UI can render a
per-clause breakdown. ``blockers`` is non-empty when ``outcome``
is ``blocked`` or ``exception``.

SimulationActionRequest.title: SimulationActionRequest
SimulationActionRequest.description:
One actor decision in the simulation script.

The actor supplies the ``transition_key`` (the transition they
would fire from the current state). ``payload`` is forwarded to
the runtime engine; the simulator does not interpret it, but
accepts and echoes it for round-trip parity with the live endpoint.

SlaStateView.title: SlaStateView
SlaStateView.description:
The wire shape of the case-summary ``sla_state`` slot.

Mirrors :class:`app.application.cases.sla_state.SlaStateSummary`.
``state`` is one of ``"breached"`` / ``"warning"`` / ``"active"``
/ ``"paused"`` / ``"completed"`` / ``"none"``. ``next_due_at`` is
the soonest ``due_at`` across the case's clocks that drove the
worst tier (``breached`` clocks show the past deadline so the
operator sees when the case went overdue). The counts break
down the case's clock set so the workspace UI can render
"1 breached, 2 active" without re-fetching.

SortEntry.title: SortEntry
SortEntry.description: A single ``(field, direction)`` sort entry on the wire.

StartFormSessionRequest.title: StartFormSessionRequest
StartFormSessionRequest.description: POST body for starting or resuming a multi-step session.

StateDefinitionRequest.title: StateDefinitionRequest
StateDefinitionRequest.description: Wire shape of a single state in a workflow version.

SubmitFormRequest.title: SubmitFormRequest
SubmitFormRequest.description: POST body for submitting a form against a case.

url.title: Url
url.description: HTTPS URL deliveries are POSTed to

secret_name.title: Secret Name
secret_name.description: Logical key into SecretProvider. The platform resolves the value through SecretProvider.get(secret_name).

require_bearer.title: Require Bearer
require_bearer.description: When true, an Authorization: Bearer <jwt> is attached

SubscriptionCreateRequest.title: SubscriptionCreateRequest
SubscriptionCreateRequest.description:
Body of ``POST /api/v1/webhooks/subscriptions``.

The shape is the application layer's
:class:`RegisterSubscriptionCommand` minus transport fields
(``tenant_id`` is taken from the authenticated caller).

SubscriptionResponse.title: SubscriptionResponse
SubscriptionResponse.description: Wire shape returned for a subscription.

version_token.title: Version Token
version_token.description: The version_token the caller observed; rejected on stale

TaskSummary.title: TaskSummary
TaskSummary.description:
Lightweight task summary embedded in transition responses.

The full task view (``TaskView``) carries completion timestamps
and audit hooks; this shape only exposes the fields a client
needs to render a follow-on-task list (P02-US1 acceptance
scenario 1).

TaskView.title: TaskView
TaskView.description:
Canonical task view (read shape for ``GET /api/v1/tasks``).

Mirrors the ``Task`` aggregate (P02-US1 / FM-014 / FR-011). The
``status`` field is the lifecycle value (``open`` / ``completed`` /
``cancelled``); ``version_token`` is the optimistic-concurrency
token (Constitution V — no silent overwrites).

TimelineEntryResponse.title: TimelineEntryResponse
TimelineEntryResponse.description: A single audit row on the timeline wire shape (P09-US1, US4).

TransitionDefinitionRequest.title: TransitionDefinitionRequest
TransitionDefinitionRequest.description:
Wire shape of a single transition in a workflow version.

``human_driven`` is the cycle-breaking flag the validator uses to
distinguish a breakable reviewer loop (``intake -> in_review ->
needs_info -> in_review``) from a runaway automatic loop (plan §5).

TransitionFormCheckRequest.title: TransitionFormCheckRequest
TransitionFormCheckRequest.description:
POST body for the transition form guard (P07-US7).

``target_state`` is the state the transition is about to land in;
``submitted_form_keys`` is the set of form_keys the case already
has submitted forms for. The endpoint returns a verdict the
workflow engine merges with its other guards.

Why ``target_state`` is in the body: the SPA can call this guard
before the user clicks "Submit" on a transition form, using the
state the form will land in. The engine's runtime call site uses
the same shape — the application validator is purely a function
over (target_state, requirements, submitted_keys).

TransitionFormCheckResponse.title: TransitionFormCheckResponse
TransitionFormCheckResponse.description: Verdict returned by the transition-form guard.

TransitionPreflight.title: TransitionPreflight
TransitionPreflight.description: Safe availability and guard verdict for one current transition.

TransitionPreflightResponse.title: TransitionPreflightResponse
TransitionPreflightResponse.description: Current workflow state and all executable transition options.

UnfreezeCaseRequest.title: UnfreezeCaseRequest
UnfreezeCaseRequest.description:
Body for ``POST /api/v1/admin/archival/cases/{case_id}/unfreeze``.

``reason`` is required and audited.

WebhookCommandResponse.title: WebhookCommandResponse
WebhookCommandResponse.description:
Wire shape returned by ``POST /api/v1/webhooks/{channel}``.

``replayed=True`` means the webhook id was already on file; the
applied_command below is the *original* capture's and no new
command was applied.

WorkflowDefinitionRequest.title: WorkflowDefinitionRequest
WorkflowDefinitionRequest.description:
The full ``definition_json`` body for a draft workflow version.

Validated by ``app.application.configuration.validate_definition``;
on failure the request returns 422 ``validation_failed`` and no row
is persisted.

WorkflowDiffResponse.title: WorkflowDiffResponse
WorkflowDiffResponse.description: Stable, read-only summary of changes from the previous version.

WorkflowStateResponse.title: WorkflowStateResponse
WorkflowStateResponse.description: Read-only state projection for the admin workflow viewer.

WorkflowSummaryResponse.title: WorkflowSummaryResponse
WorkflowSummaryResponse.description: Workflow header and its effective version pointer.

WorkflowTransitionResponse.title: WorkflowTransitionResponse
WorkflowTransitionResponse.description: Read-only transition projection for the admin workflow viewer.

WorkflowValidationResponse.title: WorkflowValidationResponse
WorkflowValidationResponse.description:
Response from ``POST /api/v1/admin/workflows/{key}/versions:validate``.

Returns the parsed ``definition_json`` snapshot so the admin UI can
render what would be published without persisting a row. The
response is intentionally small: it carries the id the admin UI
needs (workflow + queue set) and confirms the validator passed.

app__interfaces__http__schemas__admin_go.title: PublicationHistoryResponse
app__interfaces__http__schemas__admin_go.description:
The full governance timeline response.

``items`` is newest-first; the standard ``Page[T]`` envelope
(AGENTS.md §17.1) is not used here because the timeline UI
intentionally consumes the array directly to render the column.
